name: Asahikawa, Biei and Furano
tagline: The heart of Hokkaido, linking rolling hills and flower fields, a zoo and ramen
intro: This is central Hokkaido, where Asahiyama Zoo with its walking penguins, the patchwork hills of Biei and the Blue Pond, and the purple lavender of Farm Tomita in Furano in July are all within about an hour's drive of one another. In the evening you can enjoy Asahikawa soy sauce ramen and izakaya, and one day can be spent soaking in the hot springs of Sounkyo Gorge, so nature and good food alternate nicely. A rental car gives you the most freedom, but in summer the Lavender Express bus and sightseeing trains still cover the highlights, so it suits both two women traveling together and families with children.
season_notes: Spring (Apr-May): the snow is melting, so the hills are brown and the zoo closes for a stretch in mid-April; not recommended, with fresh greenery from late May. Summer (Jun-Aug): lavender peaks in mid-July and the Biei hills are at their most colorful; it is high season, so book lodging early. Autumn (Sep-Oct): the foliage at Sounkyo and Kurodake turns in mid to late September, the earliest in Japan, and the Biei fields show harvest scenery. Winter (Dec-Mar): the penguin walk (late December to mid-March) and the Blue Pond light-up are the draws, but rental car drivers need snow-driving experience and some Biei hill roads are closed.
airport_access/0/note: Runs to match arriving flights, about 40 min. The ¥750 fare is under application to rise to ¥1,100 in April 2026 (Asahikawa Denki-Kido notice), so check before boarding
airport_access/1/note: About 15 min to Biei Station and about 1 hour to Furano Station. Only a few runs a day, so check the timetable. Fare to be confirmed (around ¥400 to Biei and ¥800 to Furano, estimate)
airport_access/2/note: Biei is closer to the airport (about 15 km). Reserve the rental office in front of the airport in peak season
airport_access/3/mode: JR Rapid Airport + Limited Express Lilac or Kamui
airport_access/3/note: Change at Sapporo Station. The limited express takes about 85 min. Combined fare is around ¥5,000 (estimate, to be confirmed). Suits itineraries that pass through Sapporo
airport_access/4/note: The route that goes straight to Furano and Biei without passing through Sapporo. Expressway tolls are extra
getting_around: In Asahikawa city, walking from the station along Heiwa-dori Shopping Park reaches the famous ramen shops and izakaya, and the zoo is reached by bus from in front of the station (lines 41, 42 and 47, about 40 min). A rental car is the basic choice for Biei, Furano and Sounkyo; without one, combine the summer-only sightseeing train (Furano-Biei Norokko), the sightseeing bus from Biei Station and a taxi tour. You can cycle around the Biei hills, but there are many climbs, so renting an electric bike is better.
transport_pass: The JR Hokkaido Rail Pass (5 days, around ¥20,000) only pays off if you take the limited express both ways to Sapporo. Buses in front of Asahikawa Station accept transit IC cards, and there is practically no dedicated pass. For Biei and Furano, it is realistic to budget ¥7,000 to ¥10,000 per day for a rental car (estimate).
spots/0/desc: A small airport 20 minutes by car from the Biei hills and 35 minutes from downtown Asahikawa. The international terminal was tidied up with a 2019 extension, and the airport is known for few cancellations even in heavy snow.
spots/0/access: Direct flights from Incheon (seasonal, certain days), airport shuttle bus to Asahikawa Station in 35 min
spots/0/tip: Rental car counters are in front of the terminal, and a shuttle takes you to each office. The second-floor shop is small, so buy souvenirs in the city.
spots/0/kid_tip: From the second-floor observation deck you can watch planes take off and land with Mt. Daisetsu behind them.
spots/1/desc: Hokkaido's gateway, with many direct flights daily from Incheon, Gimhae, Daegu and elsewhere. It takes a little over 2 hours to Asahikawa by limited express with a change at Sapporo, or 2 hours by rental car to Furano, so it is used for itineraries combined with Sapporo.
spots/1/access: JR New Chitose Airport Station on basement level 1, rental car counters on level 1
spots/1/hours: International lobby always open, shops generally 8:00–20:00
spots/1/tip: When changing at Sapporo Station to the Limited Express Lilac or Kamui, unreserved seats fill up on Friday evenings and holidays, so book reserved seats in advance.
spots/1/kid_tip: The Doraemon Waku Waku Sky Park on level 3 of the domestic terminal is good for killing time.
spots/2/desc: The central station, whose glass walls and Hokkaido timber are a sight in themselves. The AEON Mall in front of the station and Heiwa-dori Shopping Park stretching to the north are lined with ramen shops, izakaya and cafes.
spots/2/access: Terminus of the Limited Express Lilac and Kamui, airport shuttle bus stop in front of the station
spots/2/tip: Buses to the zoo leave from around stop 6 in front of the station, so check the stop number the day before. Coin lockers are beside the ticket gates.
spots/2/kid_tip: Kitasaito Garden south of the station is a riverside park that is good for a stroll with a stroller.
spots/3/desc: Japan's northernmost zoo, which became famous for its behavioral exhibits that show animals acting naturally. Penguins that seem to fly through the water, polar bears passing overhead, and the winter penguin walk (late December to mid-March) are the signature sights.
spots/3/access: About 40 min by bus from Asahikawa Station, 25 min by rental car
spots/3/hours: 2026: summer season (4/29–10/15) 9:30–17:15 (last entry 16:00), 10/16–11/3 9:30–16:30, winter season (11/11–12/29) 10:30–15:30 (last entry 15:00). Night Zoo 8/10–16 until 21:00 (per travel agency information, check the official site)
spots/3/tip: The penguin walk takes place twice, at 11:00 and 14:30 (winter only), so enter right at the 10:30 opening and get a spot. The grounds are hilly, so it is easier to start at the east gate entrance and walk down.
spots/3/kid_tip: Free for junior high school students and younger. Check the feeding time (Mogu Mogu Time) board at the entrance first and plan your route around it.
spots/4/desc: A food-court style ramen theme hall where eight famous Asahikawa ramen shops share one building. It is on the way to the zoo, so it is easy to stop by, and some shops sell half sizes so you can compare two bowls.
spots/4/access: 15 min by car from Asahikawa Station, on the zoo bus route (get off at Nagayama 11-jo 4-chome)
spots/4/hours: Around 11:00–20:00 (varies by shop, to be confirmed)
spots/4/tip: The Ramen Village shrine has ramen-shaped ema prayer plaques that are popular for photos. If you avoid the lunch peak (12:00–13:00), there is almost no line.
spots/4/kid_tip: Many shops have wide table seating and children's dishes, making this the easiest ramen spot to visit with kids.
spots/5/desc: A museum of the Otokoyama sake brewery, which has continued since the Edo period. You can see sake barrels in ukiyo-e prints and old brewing tools, enjoy a free tasting, and buy sake sold only here.
spots/5/access: 15 min by car from Asahikawa Station, 5 min by car from Ramen Village
spots/5/tip: There is a spot at the entrance where you can draw the underground water from Mt. Daisetsu, so bring an empty bottle. In the winter brewing season you can also see the sake being pressed.
spots/5/kid_tip: Tasting is for adults only. Kids can have non-alcoholic amazake and sake lees soft serve ice cream.
spots/6/desc: Japan's first pedestrian-only shopping street, running 1 km north from Asahikawa Station. Ramen shops, izakaya, department stores and drugstores gather along this street and the side alleys on both sides (Sanrokugai), so dinner and shopping can both be finished here.
spots/6/access: Right at the north exit of Asahikawa Station
spots/6/tip: In early February, ice sculptures line this street during the Asahikawa Winter Festival. The Sanrokugai side is a nightlife district, so avoid walking alone late at night.
spots/6/kid_tip: There are many sculptures and benches in the middle of the street, so kids can rest easily.
spots/7/desc: An English-style garden cultivated for Hokkaido's climate, with a hill made famous by a TV drama (Sayaka's Hill) and a cafe. It is 10 minutes by car from the zoo, so it pairs well with a zoo visit.
spots/7/access: 10 min by car from Asahiyama Zoo
spots/7/hours: Late April to mid-October 10:00–17:00 (to be confirmed)
spots/7/closed: Closed in winter (cafe partly open, to be confirmed)
spots/7/tip: Roses and perennials peak from late June through July. The chiffon cake at the garden-side cafe NAYA is popular.
spots/7/kid_tip: There is a notice that children of junior high school age and younger enter free, but this is to be confirmed. The garden paths are flat, so strollers are fine.
spots/8/desc: A small stone station built of Biei tuff, where the hill tour buses, taxis and rental bicycles all depart from the station front. The buildings on the street in front are unified with stone and triangular roofs, so the town itself is a photo subject.
spots/8/access: About 35 min by JR Furano Line from Asahikawa Station, 20 min by car from Asahikawa Airport
spots/8/tip: At the Shikisai Information Center (tourist office) in front of the station, check that day's hill road closures and bus times. Leave bags in the coin lockers beside the office.
spots/8/kid_tip: The sightseeing bus from the station front uses reserved seating, so book ahead if you have kids.
spots/9/desc: A complex run by JA Biei combining a farm produce shop, bakery and restaurant. You can buy bread made with Biei wheat and vegetables harvested that day, such as corn and asparagus.
spots/9/access: 10 min on foot from Biei Station, 3 min by car
spots/9/hours: Around 9:00–17:00 (varies by season, to be confirmed)
spots/9/closed: New Year holidays, some facilities closed in winter (to be confirmed)
spots/9/tip: The Biei corn bread often sells out in the morning, so stop here before the hill tour.
spots/9/kid_tip: You can have a quick snack of soft serve ice cream and bread at the outdoor tables.
spots/10/name: Patchwork Road and the Ken and Mary Tree
spots/10/desc: A scenic drive through the hills of northwest Biei, where the fields link like a patchwork quilt. The Ken and Mary Tree from a TV commercial, the Seven Stars Tree, and the Parent and Child Tree stand scattered across the land, with Mt. Daisetsu in the distance.
spots/10/access: Starts 10 min by car from Biei Station, by rental car or sightseeing bus
spots/10/tip: All the trees stand in private fields, so do not step off the road. To avoid backlight in the morning, the Patchwork Road is best in the afternoon and the Panorama Road in the morning.
spots/10/kid_tip: This course involves little time out of the car, so let kids run around at Hokuseinooka Viewing Park.
spots/11/desc: A single oak tree made famous when it appeared on a cigarette package in 1976. A row of birch trees lines up beside it, making it a classic composition for Patchwork Road photos.
spots/11/access: 5 min by car from the Ken and Mary Tree
spots/11/tip: The parking lot is small, so avoid 10:00–11:00 when large buses crowd in. In winter, the lone tree on the snowfield is even more impressive.
spots/12/desc: A park where a pyramid-shaped observation tower gives you the whole Patchwork Road and the Tokachidake mountain range in one view. In summer, lavender and sunflowers bloom in the front garden, and the stand sells corn and potatoes.
spots/12/access: 7 min by car from Biei Station, 25 min by bicycle
spots/12/tip: There is a tourist information desk, so it is a good starting point to pick up a Patchwork Road map.
spots/12/kid_tip: The lawn is wide and good for resting with a snack. Kids especially love the steamed corn.
spots/13/desc: Biei's largest flower garden, where colorful bands of flowers cover 15 hectares of gentle hills. You can ride around on a tractor bus or cart, and in winter it turns into a field for snowmobiles and sledding, with an alpaca farm attached.
spots/13/access: 25 min on foot from JR Bibaushi Station, 12 min by car from Biei Station
spots/13/hours: May and Oct 8:40–17:00, Jun–Sep 8:40–17:30, Nov–Dec 9:10–16:30, Jan 8:40–16:30, Feb–Apr 9:10–17:00 (per March 2026 information, to be confirmed)
spots/13/closed: None (New Year holidays to be confirmed)
spots/13/tip: Admission is ¥500 for adults and ¥300 for children from July to September, and free in other months (to be confirmed). The alpaca farm costs extra: ¥500 for high school students and older, ¥300 for elementary and junior high students. The flowers are fullest from mid-July through August, and the September cosmos are also lovely.
spots/13/kid_tip: Kids can feed the alpacas at the alpaca farm (extra fee). Cart rental requires a guardian to drive.
spots/14/desc: A triangular spruce standing alone in the middle of a wide field. The snow-covered winter scene looks just like a Christmas card, as the name says, and it is the symbol of winter photos in Biei.
spots/14/access: 5 min by car from Shikisai Hill
spots/14/tip: Do not enter the field; the rule is to shoot from the roadside with a telephoto lens. When stopping at the roadside in winter, take care not to get stuck in the snow.
spots/15/desc: An artificial pond created by volcanic disaster-prevention works, it looks blue because of its aluminum content and has dead trees standing in it, and became known worldwide as an Apple wallpaper. From November to April, the evening light-up shows a completely different face.
spots/15/access: 20 min by car from Biei Station, about 20 min by Dohoku Bus line 39 bound for Shirogane Onsen (a few runs a day)
spots/15/hours: Always open. Parking lot 7:00–19:00 May–Oct, 8:00–21:30 Nov–Apr. Light-up runs in the evenings from late October to late April (2025–26 season 10/24–4/22, 2026–27 season start date to be confirmed)
spots/15/tip: Parking is ¥1,000 for cars (rising July 1, 2026; ¥300 for motorcycles). It is bluest on a clear morning with no wind and looks gray when cloudy, so swap the order of your stops depending on the weather. The Blue Pond soft serve ice cream at the stand is the specialty.
spots/15/kid_tip: The path around the pond is a flat 300 m dirt trail, so strollers are fine.
spots/16/desc: A waterfall where groundwater splits like a white beard and drops from gaps in a cliff, and the Biei River flowing below has the same blue color as the Blue Pond. The standard view is looking down from the bridge.
spots/16/access: 5 min by car from the Blue Pond, 3 min on foot from the Shirogane Onsen bus terminal
spots/16/hours: Always open (winter evening light-up, to be confirmed)
spots/16/tip: The bridge is narrow, so wait a moment for large buses to leave before taking photos. In winter, frost on the bridge railing makes it even prettier.
spots/16/kid_tip: The bridge railing is high, so hold young children up to see.
spots/17/desc: A small hot spring village in the forest at the foot of Tokachidake, named for a bath said to be so good for rheumatism that you could forget your cane. It is right next to the Blue Pond, so it combines well with a day-use bath, and each inn has an open-air bath.
spots/17/access: 5 min by car from the Blue Pond
spots/17/hours: Day-use bathing around 13:00–20:00 depending on the inn (to be confirmed)
spots/17/tip: Day-use bath fees are around ¥1,000 (estimate). The open-air bath at the Park Hills Hotel is famous for its forest view. Towel rental costs extra.
spots/18/desc: At 1,280 m above sea level, this is the highest hot spring in Hokkaido, where you see the Tokachidake ridge and a sea of clouds from an iron-rich brown open-air bath. Late September foliage comes down right to the front of the open-air bath.
spots/18/access: 30 min by car from Kamifurano Station, 30 min by car (mountain road) from the Blue Pond
spots/18/tip: Fees are rough figures as of 2024. It is a mountain road, so chains and 4WD are needed in winter. Soap use is restricted at this natural hot spring, so wash up at your inn.
spots/18/kid_tip: The bath is on the hot side, so keep young children's soak short. On the way there is also the Fukiage open-air bath (free, mixed bathing), but it is not for families.
spots/19/desc: The original lavender farm of Furano, where purple slopes and rainbow-colored flower beds peak in mid-July, and admission is free. With lavender soft serve ice cream, a distillery workshop and a dried flower house, it is worth a visit even in seasons without flowers.
spots/19/access: 7 min on foot from JR Lavender-batake Station (summer-only temporary station), 25 min on foot from Nakafurano Station, 40 min by car from Biei
spots/19/hours: 8:30–18:00 (varies by season, per 2024 information, to be confirmed)
spots/19/tip: In 2026, full bloom was reported on July 13, with the peak from mid-July to early August. From 10:00 to 15:00 there are days when the parking wait exceeds an hour, so arrive before 9:00.
spots/19/kid_tip: The paths between the fields are dirt, so a baby carrier is easier than a stroller. Have a snack of cut melon at the Melon House.
spots/20/desc: A small station where the Furano Line and the Nemuro Main Line meet, with Furano Marche and omelet curry restaurants within walking distance. In summer, the Norokko sightseeing train to Biei departs from here.
spots/20/access: About 70 min by JR from Asahikawa Station, 40 min by car from Biei
spots/20/tip: A bus from in front of the station reaches Ningle Terrace (New Furano Prince Hotel) in 15 min. In winter, parts of the Nemuro Main Line have schedule changes, so check.
spots/21/desc: A market complex with Furano produce, processed foods, desserts and takeout shops, in two buildings (1 and 2). You can buy Furano melon, cheese, pudding and wine in one place and eat them on the outdoor plaza.
spots/21/access: 7 min on foot from Furano Station
spots/21/hours: Around 10:00–19:00 (shorter in winter, to be confirmed)
spots/21/tip: Furano milk pudding and melon bread are popular as gifts. Stop by lightly for a snack before dinner.
spots/21/kid_tip: The plaza has many benches, and there are restrooms and a nursing room.
spots/22/desc: A craft village where 15 log-cabin workshops line a wooden deck path through the forest, created by the TV drama writer Kuramoto Sou. When the sun sets, lanterns are lit and it becomes a fairy-tale scene, and a snowy winter night is the prettiest.
spots/22/access: 15 min by bus or 10 min by car from Furano Station, inside the New Furano Prince Hotel
spots/22/hours: 12:00–20:45 (from 10:00 in peak summer, to be confirmed)
spots/22/closed: Maintenance closure sometime in November (to be confirmed)
spots/22/tip: Enter 30 minutes before sunset to see both the day and night scenery. The nearby Forest Clock cafe uses the drama set as it was.
spots/22/kid_tip: The deck has steps, so strollers are awkward. Each workshop offers small gifts for kids such as little bells and music boxes.
spots/23/desc: A cheese factory in the forest where you watch the production process through glass and sample wine cheese and camembert. On the same grounds are a pizza workshop, an ice milk workshop and a hall for butter and cheese making experiences.
spots/23/access: 10 min by car from Furano Station
spots/23/tip: Experiences (making butter or ice cream) are registered on the day, but in peak season they fill up in the morning. The pizza workshop is good as a lunch substitute.
spots/23/kid_tip: Elementary school students can do the experiences alone; preschoolers need a guardian. There is a lawn and play equipment.
spots/24/desc: A city-run winery that offers aging cellar tours and free tastings, and being on a hill it has fine views of Furano town and Tokachidake. Lavender blooms on the front slope from late June to July.
spots/24/access: 7 min by car from Furano Station, next to Campana Rokkatei
spots/24/tip: Drivers cannot taste. Besides wine, Furano grape juice is good for kids and as a gift.
spots/25/desc: A glass-walled shop and cafe that the Hokkaido confectioner Rokkatei built on a vineyard hill, where you eat Marusei butter sandwiches and grape desserts sold only here while looking at Tokachidake. It handles shopping and rest in one stop.
spots/25/access: 7 min by car from Furano Station
spots/25/hours: Around 10:00–16:00 (varies by season, to be confirmed)
spots/25/closed: Closed for a period in winter (to be confirmed)
spots/25/tip: Coffee inside the shop is free. The grape soft serve ice cream is available only here.
spots/25/kid_tip: The window seats are wide and there are high chairs for kids.
spots/26/desc: A hot spring village inside a gorge in Daisetsuzan National Park, with hotels and open-air baths gathered beneath columnar-jointed cliffs. During the Ice Waterfall Festival from late January to mid-March, ice sculptures and fireworks are added.
spots/26/access: 1 hour 30 min by car from Asahikawa Station, about 2 hours by Dohoku Bus bound for Sounkyo (a few runs a day)
spots/26/hours: Day-use bathing around 12:00–20:00 depending on the facility (to be confirmed), Kurodake-no-Yu around 10:00–20:00 (to be confirmed)
spots/26/tip: For a day-use bath, the public Kurodake-no-Yu (around ¥600, to be confirmed) is convenient. If staying overnight, the right order is a gorge walk and open-air bath in the evening, then the ropeway in the morning.
spots/26/kid_tip: The foot bath in the village is free. The Ice Waterfall Festival is cold at night, so dress fully for the cold.
spots/27/desc: In 7 minutes it lifts you from Sounkyo to a plateau at 1,300 m above sea level, and a chairlift connects you onward to the 7th station. The foliage in mid-September is the earliest in Japan, and the mountain turns into alpine flowers in summer and snowy scenery and a ski area in winter.
spots/27/access: 5 min on foot from the Sounkyo hot spring town
spots/27/hours: Around 6:00–18:00 (summer), 8:00–16:00 (winter), varies by season (to be confirmed)
spots/27/closed: Maintenance closures in spring and autumn (to be confirmed)
spots/27/tip: The ropeway plus chairlift set round trip is ¥3,900 for adults and ¥1,950 for elementary students (per 2025–2026 information). The ropeway-only fare is to be confirmed. It is nearly 10 degrees colder at the top, so bring a jacket even in summer. Closures for strong wind are frequent, so ride early in the morning.
spots/27/kid_tip: Around the 5th station there is an observation deck and a short trail, so kids can manage without strain. The chairlift has no safety bar, so hold young children on your lap.
spots/28/desc: Two waterfalls that drop side by side from a cliff; the thin Ginga (Milky Way) is called the female fall and the thick Ryusei (Meteor) the male fall. A 20-minute climb from the parking lot brings you to a viewpoint that frames both falls in one shot.
spots/28/access: 5 min by car from Sounkyo hot spring town
spots/28/closed: Viewpoint trail closed in winter (to be confirmed)
spots/28/tip: The viewpoint trail is a steep dirt path, so sneakers are a must. At the stand beside the parking lot, try the bite-size yaki dango, a Sounkyo specialty.
spots/28/kid_tip: Both falls can be seen well from the parking lot too, so you can skip the viewpoint.
spots/29/desc: A forest garden set against Mt. Daisetsu, and along with Ueno Farm a leading garden on the Hokkaido Garden Route. With a restaurant and villas in the garden, it is a good lunch stop on the way to Sounkyo.
spots/29/access: 15 min by car from Sounkyo, 1 hour 10 min by car from Asahikawa
spots/29/hours: Late April to mid-October 9:00–17:00 (to be confirmed)
spots/29/tip: Fees are rough figures as of 2024. Perennials in July and August and foliage in late September are best, and a misty morning has a lovely atmosphere.
spots/29/kid_tip: There is a forest playground area where kids can run around.
restaurants/0/desc: Founded in 1947 and considered the originator of Asahikawa ramen, its pork bone and fish broth topped with burnt lard has a slightly bitter aroma. The strong flavor divides opinion, so go in the spirit of tasting the history of Asahikawa ramen.
restaurants/1/desc: A third-generation shop that has run since 1947, serving clear, clean soy sauce ramen with a double broth of pork bone, chicken and bonito. It is a 5-minute walk from the station, so it is the safest choice for a first meal after arrival.
restaurants/1/tips/1: Few seats, best for groups of 2 to 3
restaurants/2/desc: Founded in 1969, it serves rich soy sauce ramen with layered pork bone and seafood broth, the most mainstream taste among the three great Asahikawa ramen masters. It is in a basement but has plenty of seats, so it is comfortable for families too.
restaurants/2/tips/2: Check whether credit cards are accepted
restaurants/3/desc: The main shop of Santouka, which has many branches overseas, famous for salt ramen in a milky pork bone broth topped with a single pickled plum. A good choice when you want a mild flavor in soy-sauce-centered Asahikawa, or when going with kids.
restaurants/3/tips/2: 5 min on foot from the station
restaurants/4/desc: Founded in 1952, it serves rich soy sauce ramen with a moderate layer of lard, often named by locals. The line of tourists is short, so you can eat at a relaxed pace.
restaurants/4/tips/1: The fried rice set is popular
restaurants/5/desc: Asahikawa's leading Western-style restaurant, open since 1939, serving katsu curry with an old department store dining hall feel, menchi katsu (minced meat cutlet) and omurice. When you are tired of ramen, the menu satisfies the whole family.
restaurants/5/tips/2: Table seating on the second floor
restaurants/6/desc: A famous Asahikawa Genghis Khan restaurant that grills fresh young lamb, not frozen, over charcoal, with almost no gamey smell, which makes it good for a first taste of lamb. You can eat your fill for around ¥3,000 per person.
restaurants/6/tips/1: Smoke clings to clothes, so take off your jacket
restaurants/7/desc: A long-established Asahikawa izakaya running since 1946, famous for shinkoyaki, a whole young chicken grilled, along with Hokkaido mountain vegetables and local sake. With counter and tatami seating, both atmosphere and flavor are reliable.
restaurants/7/tips/1: Shinkoyaki takes time, so order it first
restaurants/8/signature: Jibiru (local beer) set and Genghis Khan
restaurants/8/desc: In a brick building converted from an old warehouse, it serves Asahikawa craft beer, Genghis Khan and dishes made with Hokkaido ingredients. It is spacious and lively, so families with kids can also spend a relaxed evening.
restaurants/8/tips/0: 5 min on foot from the station
restaurants/9/signature: Kibana (almond diamond cookies) and soft serve ice cream
restaurants/9/desc: The factory-run shop and cafe of Tsuboya, which makes Asahikawa's signature confection 'Kibana', with a lovely garden and glass-walled lounge. A good place to pick out gifts and rest with a cup of coffee.
restaurants/9/tips/0: 10 min by car from the station
restaurants/10/desc: A set-meal restaurant in front of Biei Station, where katsu curry made with Biei pork and ramen are popular. It is easy to eat at without fuss before or after a hill tour, and the portions are generous.
restaurants/11/desc: A French restaurant inside Biei Senka serving a course centered on Biei vegetables, supervised by a well-known Sapporo chef. It is popular with women travelers as a special lunch that matches the hill scenery.
restaurants/11/hours: Around 11:00–15:00, 17:00–20:00 (varies by season, to be confirmed)
restaurants/11/closed: Wednesday and the winter closure period (to be confirmed)
restaurants/12/signature: Biei wagyu hamburg steak and steak
restaurants/12/desc: A restaurant run directly by the ranch that raises Biei wagyu, where you eat hamburg steak and steak while looking at the hills through glass walls. The animal plaza next door (feeding goats and sheep) makes it the best lunch spot with kids.
restaurants/12/hours: Around 11:00–20:00 (shorter in winter, to be confirmed)
restaurants/12/tips/2: 15 min by car from Biei Station
restaurants/13/signature: Natural yeast bread and cheese souffle
restaurants/13/desc: A forest cafe on a hill in Bibaushi, famous for natural yeast bread baked in a wood-fired oven and souffle. It is close to Shikisai Hill, so it is a good afternoon break.
restaurants/13/tips/0: Bread often sells out in the afternoon
restaurants/14/signature: Omelet curry and homemade sausage curry
restaurants/14/desc: The symbol of Furano curry, open since 1974, known for curry topped with homemade sausage and omelet curry. There is a fun tradition where you call out for a roux refill and get more.
restaurants/14/tips/0: Long waits, so arrive before opening
restaurants/15/desc: The most down-to-earth neighborhood diner among the certified Furano omelet curry shops, which follows the rule of using local rice, vegetables and milk. Prices are low and the menu is varied, so family members can each eat something different.
restaurants/16/signature: Wagyu roast beef bowl and mountain vegetable hotpot
restaurants/16/desc: A long-established Furano izakaya also known as a filming location of the drama 'From the Northern Country', serving local dishes such as a wagyu roast beef bowl and venison or duck hotpot. It is the best place to get the Furano atmosphere at dinner.
restaurants/16/tips/1: 5 min on foot from Furano Station
restaurants/16/tips/2: The lunch bowl is good value
restaurants/17/desc: Pizza baked in a wood-fired oven with cheese made at the cheese factory, around ¥1,500 per pie. Lunch on a forest terrace is a big hit with kids.

hotels/0/pts/0: Connected to the station and AEON Mall

bplan/0/desc: When rain or a snowstorm keeps you off the hills, it is 15 minutes from the city. Sake brewing exhibits, tasting and small gift bottles make an hour pass quickly.
bplan/1/desc: For when the zoo is closed (mid-April, early November) or you have time left after the zoo. 10 minutes by car from the zoo, an English-style garden and cafe open only May to October.
bplan/2/desc: On the way to Sounkyo, or when you have half a day left from Asahikawa. A forest garden walk and a viewing cafe, open late April to mid-October.
bplan/3/desc: With kids, choose butter and ice cream making (registered on the day) and the pizza workshop instead of flower fields. All indoors, even in rain.
bplan/4/desc: If you have a rental car and the weather is clear, go 20 more minutes up the mountain road from Shirogane for a day-use bath at Hokkaido's highest hot spring. Open-air bath above the clouds (to be confirmed).
bplan/5/desc: When the hills are hidden by rain or fog, an indoor market next to Biei Station. Half a day with Biei wheat bread, corn and cheese snacks, and a meal at Asperges.
bplan/6/desc: A sea-of-clouds viewpoint reached by gondola at dawn, 1 hour south of Furano by rental car (May to October). Whether the clouds appear is a matter of luck, so check the forecast the day before (to be confirmed).
bplan/7/desc: On days when heavy snow or strong wind blocks the ropeway or hills, handle it in the city. Compare two shops at Ramen Village, then shop and have a cafe at AEON Mall connected to the station.
